iut_type: End Product (Shimano cycling computer/peripheral), self-administered PTS testing scope confirmation
customer_question: We're developing a product using an already Bluetooth-registered radio chip, and plan to extract and self-test in-house only the items not already covered by that chip's registration, before submitting our report to you. Our product supports BAS and DIS as its only SIG-standard services (no SIG-defined profiles like Cycling Power Profile, no LE Audio/Mesh/Traditional Profiles), using LE Secure Connections Pairing as a change from our past models. Since the Core Specification is already tested via the chip's registered ICS, is our understanding correct that we only need to self-test the BAS/DIS items?
question_variants: Is Core Protocol testing fully exempted by referencing the chip's existing registration?
Do we only need to self-test BAS and DIS specifically, or is anything else required?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to confirm, before investing effort in self-administered PTS testing, that their understanding of which test items were already covered by the chip's existing registration (exempting Core Protocol layers) versus which items genuinely needed to be self-tested (BAS and DIS) was accurate.
plain_english_explanation: Core Protocol layers are exempted from testing by referencing the chip's existing Host Subsystem and Controller Subsystem registrations (specifically, an NCS Host v2.8.0 registration and a corresponding LE Core-Controller registration). However, if the radio chip itself is implemented as a bare SoC, RF PHY testing covering the 1Mbps and 2Mbps modes that chip's QDID supports is still required; if instead the customer implements the chip via a packaged module (such as a Kaga FEI module built around the same chip), referencing that module's own QDID/DN would exempt RF PHY testing entirely. Separately, the customer's understanding that DIS and BAS profile testing must be self-administered (since these aren't covered by the chip's Core Protocol registration) was confirmed as correct.
consultant_answer: Yes, your Core Protocol layers are exempted by referencing the chip's existing Host Subsystem (NCS Host v2.8.0) and Controller Subsystem registrations. However, if you implement the chip as a bare SoC, RF PHY testing for the 1Mbps and 2Mbps modes that QDID supports is still required — if you instead implement it via a packaged module (like one from Kaga FEI built on the same chip), referencing that module's own QDID/DN would exempt RF PHY testing entirely. Your understanding that DIS and BAS profile testing need to be self-administered is correct, since these aren't covered by the chip's Core Protocol registration.
decision_logic: Test scope for a product implementing an already-registered radio chip should be broken down by layer: Core Protocol exemption via the chip's Host/Controller registration applies regardless of bare-SoC vs. module implementation, but RF PHY test exemption specifically depends on whether a packaged module's own QDID/DN can be referenced instead of the bare chip's.
final_recommendation: When confirming a customer's self-test scope assumption, explicitly verify each layer separately (Core Protocol via chip registration, RF PHY depending on bare-chip vs. module implementation, and profile-layer items needing self-testing) rather than giving a single blanket confirmation.
risk_if_done_wrong: Confirming the customer's self-test scope assumption without checking the bare-chip-vs-module distinction for RF PHY exemption could leave the customer believing RF PHY testing was unnecessary when implementing the chip directly as an SoC.
